answer: An farming party as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 44 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. The canyon counter is kept in crystal and mirror shows each reset. A bond is refunded only after 44 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 247 aliases cost 228 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
